explain.reason: The radar is the main sensor of an M1/N1 AEBS, so its installed detection, collision-warning, braking-request and failure-reporting functions contribute directly to vehicle compliance.
The sensor's electronic braking requests and failure behaviour must be integrated without compromising the safety and performance of the M1/N1 vehicle braking system.
The powered radar transceiver, microcontroller and CAN-FD interface constitute an electronic subassembly subject to applicable electromagnetic-emission and immunity requirements.

The software-controlled sensor communicates over CAN-FD and influences emergency braking, making its communication interfaces and security risks relevant to the M1/N1 vehicle's cybersecurity assessment and protections.
Where the vehicle permits software updates, updates affecting the radar's embedded collision-avoidance software must be covered by the vehicle's software-update management and safety requirements.
The radar, plastic radome and rigid mounting bracket behind the front emblem can affect front-end stiffness and pedestrian-impact performance of the applicable M1/N1 vehicle.
For vehicles within its passenger-car/light-truck scope, the behind-emblem sensor package and bracket must be considered in the front-end pedestrian-impact performance addressed by this GTR.
On the M1 version, the radome and front-emblem installation must preserve compliance with external-projection requirements wherever the assembly forms an accessible exterior surface.

On the M1 version, the behind-emblem installation and its brake-control interface must not cause low-speed front-protective-device impacts to compromise the braking functions protected by this regulation.
Its AEBS scope covers M2, M3, N2 and N3 vehicles, whereas the specified applications are M1 and N1 and are covered by UN R152.
The specified emergency-braking function does not provide the sustained lateral and longitudinal vehicle control of an Automated Lane Keeping System.
The specification describes an emergency intervention system, not a Driver Control Assistance System providing sustained driving assistance.
The optical warning is directed to the driver through the instrument cluster, and no exterior lighting or light-signalling device is specified.
The plastic radar radome is not safety glazing installed as a windscreen, pane or partition.
Its scope directly covers aftermarket replacement airbag modules and replacement steering wheels equipped with approved airbag modules for M1 and N1 vehicles.
The replacement rim, spokes, hub and spline connection form part of the vehicle's steering equipment and must preserve compliant steering operation when installed.

The electrical igniter and clock-spring connection interface with the existing airbag control unit, requiring integration that preserves electromagnetic compatibility and immunity of the safety-related restraint function.

The replacement airbag and steering wheel form part of the frontal-impact protective system and must preserve its required occupant-protection performance on M1 vehicles up to 3,500 kg and N1 vehicles.

For M1 vehicles up to 3,500 kg and N1 vehicles up to 2,500 kg, the replacement wheel and driver airbag must preserve the installed restraint system's compliance with frontal-collision protection requirements.
The replacement steering-wheel rim and spokes must not compromise the driver's required visibility and legibility of the installed speedometer.
The specified module introduces no ECU, network interface or cybersecurity functionality; an electrical squib connection alone does not establish component-specific cybersecurity requirements.
No software or software-update capability is specified for the replacement wheel or airbag module.
The steering wheel and driver airbag are interior equipment, not external projections.
No steering lock or other device for protection against unauthorized use is supplied or specified as being modified.
The horn switch does not bring the assembly within requirements for vehicle sound during normal driving, and the pyrotechnic inflator operates during a collision rather than normal driving.

The permanently fitted 12 V alarm for an M1 car, including intrusion detection, acoustic and optical warnings, arming/disarming and vehicle integration, falls directly within its vehicle-alarm approval scope.

The alarm ECU, electronic sensors, battery-backed siren and CAN interface must meet applicable electromagnetic compatibility requirements as electrical/electronic equipment integrated into an M1 vehicle.
Using the vehicle's direction indicators for the optical alarm brings their electrical connections and alarm-related operation within the M1 lighting-installation requirements.
The direction-indicator lamps used for the optical alarm must have compliant device approval under this consolidated light-signalling regulation rather than the older UN R6 provisions.
The CAN-connected alarm ECU and its interface with key-operated central locking must be addressed within the M1 vehicle's cybersecurity risk assessment and protective measures.
Its relevant vehicle-alarm provisions are addressed through the dedicated UN R163 approval route selected here, rather than selecting the older alarm provisions again.

The product detects intrusion and raises an alarm but contains no steering, transmission or other device that prevents unauthorized vehicle use; central-locking coordination alone does not establish that function.
The specification explicitly excludes engine immobilisation and identifies the immobilizer as a separate system.
Software-update capability is not specified, and an electronic ECU with CAN communication alone does not establish applicability of software-update requirements.
The siren provides an anti-intrusion alarm, whereas this regulation addresses vehicle sound during normal driving rather than alarm-siren performance.

The 50 mm microprismatic contour-marking tape is Class C retro-reflective marking material subject to requirements for optical performance, colour, durability and approval marking under this regulation, which consolidates UN R104.

Applying full contour markings to the sides and rear of an O4 semi-trailer requires compliance with this regulation’s installation requirements for conspicuity markings, including colour, positioning, extent and visibility.
Its scope directly covers the marking tape, but UN R150 consolidates its provisions and is selected instead.
The product is contour-marking material rather than a discrete retro-reflector, and UN R3 is also consolidated into UN R150.
The tape passively retro-reflects external illumination and contains none of the light-signalling lamps covered by this regulation.
The film and adhesive contain no electrical or electronic devices that would introduce electromagnetic compatibility requirements.
Although applied externally, the tape is fitted to an O4 semi-trailer, whereas this regulation covers external projections of M1 vehicles only.
The EPS column forms part of the M1 vehicle's steering equipment, whose steering performance, electronic control safety and operation following assistance failure must satisfy this regulation.

The electric motor, sensors, ECU and CAN interface are electrical/electronic equipment subject to applicable electromagnetic emissions and immunity requirements, particularly because interference could affect steering assistance.

For M1 vehicles within its mass scope, the collapsible column and intermediate shaft must be integrated to support compliance with frontal-impact requirements, including steering-control displacement and driver protection.
For M1 vehicles within its mass scope, the column's collapse behaviour and interaction with the steering wheel influence compliance with frontal-impact occupant-protection requirements.
The safety-critical EPS ECU and its CAN communications must be addressed by the M1 vehicle's cybersecurity risk assessment and applicable protective measures.

Where the host vehicle permits software updates, updates to the specified EPS control software must be covered by applicable software-update management and assessment of effects on steering type approval.
The specified 12 V steering-assistance motor is not an electric propulsion power train, and no traction battery or propulsion electrical equipment is specified.
The specification expressly excludes automated steering functions and contains no Automated Lane Keeping System.
Driver-commanded power assistance alone is not a Driver Control Assistance System, and no automated lateral or longitudinal control function is specified.
No steering lock or other device for preventing unauthorized vehicle use is included in the specified column.
The component is a steering column, not an aftermarket replacement airbag module or an airbag-equipped replacement steering wheel.
This consolidated regulation covers M1 front fog lamps, including requirements for the white beam, integrated LED module, electronic driver and plastic lens.
The pair of front fog lamps on an M1 vehicle must meet installation requirements concerning position, visibility, orientation, electrical switching and tell-tales.
The electronic constant-current LED driver connected to the vehicle's 12 V harness brings the lamp assembly within electromagnetic-compatibility requirements.
The lamp's exposed lens and any accessible housing edges in the M1 vehicle's front fascia must satisfy applicable external-projection requirements.
Integration into the lower front fascia must account for the low-speed protective-device impact requirements, including applicable post-impact lighting functionality.
The lower-front-fascia lamp, rigid heat sink and mounting bracket can affect pedestrian leg-impact performance and must be considered in the M1 vehicle's pedestrian-safety assessment.
The lower-front-fascia assembly can influence the vehicle-level pedestrian leg-impact performance addressed by this GTR, rather than requiring a standalone lamp approval.
Although it directly covers front fog lamps, its provisions are consolidated into UN R149, which is selected instead.
No standardized Annex 1 LED light-source category is specified; the soldered, non-replaceable LED module is assessed within the lamp under UN R149.
Its scope explicitly excludes glazing for lighting and light-signalling devices, so the polycarbonate lamp lens is not covered.
The specified device provides front fog road illumination, not any of the listed light-signalling functions such as rear fog lighting.
The specification identifies no software or software-update capability that would bring the lamp's integration within software-update requirements.

The aftermarket slip-on is a non-original replacement exhaust-silencing component for an L3 motorcycle, directly subject to requirements covering noise performance, absorptive materials, construction and approval markings.

If the motorcycle has a positive-ignition engine, integration of this exhaust-path component must preserve its applicable gaseous-emission compliance even though the catalytic converter and engine settings remain unchanged.
Its vehicle-noise requirements cover categories M and N, not the specified L3 motorcycle.
The silencer is not a replacement pollution-control device, leaves the catalytic converter unchanged, and is intended for a vehicle outside the related UN R83 categories.
The specified silencer is entirely passive and contains no electrical or electronic device requiring electromagnetic-compatibility assessment.
Although the silencer and bracket are exterior parts, this regulation covers external projections of M1 vehicles rather than L3 motorcycles.
No lighting device, shared lighting mounting or alteration to lighting installation is specified, so the rear location alone does not establish applicability.
The fascia, energy absorber, steel beam and crash boxes provide the M1 car’s low-speed rear protection and must satisfy the regulation’s installed-vehicle impact-performance requirements.
The rear steel cross-member and crash boxes influence rear-impact deformation and must be integrated so that the M1 vehicle meets rear-end collision requirements.
The exposed fascia, diffuser, tow-eye cover, sensors and reflectors must satisfy the applicable M1 external-projection requirements concerning potentially injurious shapes, edges and protrusions.
The two red Class IA retro-reflectors are explicitly within the consolidated regulation’s scope and must meet its device-performance requirements.
The two rear retro-reflectors must be installed on the M1 vehicle with the required number, colour, position, orientation and geometric visibility.

The powered ultrasonic sensors and their electrical connection to the parking-assistance ECU require assessment against applicable electromagnetic-compatibility requirements for electronic assemblies and their vehicle integration.
The ECU-connected parking sensors form part of the M1 vehicle’s electronic architecture and must be addressed in its vehicle-level cybersecurity risk assessment and applicable protective measures.
Its retro-reflector provisions are consolidated into UN R150, which is selected instead.
Its pedestrian-impact requirements concern the vehicle’s front-end impact areas, not this rear bumper assembly.
The assembly contains passive retro-reflectors, not any of the light-signalling lamps covered by this regulation.
The specified sensors provide reversing obstacle detection, not the forward-collision detection and automatic braking functions covered by this regulation.
No software-update capability is specified for the vehicle or parking-assistance system, so ECU connectivity alone does not establish applicability.
This vehicle-level regulation directly covers safety-belt reminders at all five seating positions of the M1 car, including belt-status detection and escalating visual and audible warnings.
The 12 V sensors, buckle-switch circuits, electronic evaluation and warning outputs must meet applicable electromagnetic compatibility requirements as integrated into the vehicle.
Integration of the electronic reminder into the M1 vehicle's body control unit brings its interfaces and warning-function integrity within the vehicle-level cybersecurity assessment.
If the vehicle permits software updates, updates affecting the reminder evaluation function in the body control unit must satisfy the applicable vehicle-level software-update requirements.
The interior belt-status tell-tales are not any of the exterior light-signalling devices listed in this regulation's scope.
Installation of interior safety-belt reminder indicators is not governed by the exterior lighting and light-signalling installation requirements.
Using vehicle speed to escalate a warning does not make the reminder a speedometer or odometer or establish a modification to that equipment.
The specified system detects belt use and issues warnings rather than restraining occupants, and no modification affecting frontal-impact restraint performance is specified.
Operation on the 12 V electrical system does not make the reminder electric-powertrain or rechargeable-energy-storage equipment covered by this regulation.

The laminated glass/PVB windscreen is directly covered by safety-glazing requirements, and its installation in the M1 vehicle must also meet this regulation's applicable optical and installation provisions.
The windscreen's exposed perimeter and plastic edge trim form part of the M1 vehicle's exterior and must satisfy applicable external-projection requirements.

The windscreen and its supporting perimeter affect pedestrian head-impact performance and must meet the applicable requirements where included in the test area under the amendment series used for vehicle approval.

The body-bonded windscreen and adhesive joint form part of the forward vehicle structure whose integration must support frontal-collision occupant protection, subject to the regulation's vehicle-mass scope.

The bonded windscreen's structural contribution and potential interaction with occupants must be compatible with the vehicle's frontal-impact protective-system performance, subject to the regulation's vehicle-mass scope.
Its bonnet-and-bumper pedestrian impact provisions do not directly prescribe windscreen performance; proximity to those test regions alone does not establish a separate requirement for this assembly.
The windscreen has no heating wires, antennas, electronics or other electrical functions requiring electromagnetic-compatibility assessment.
The specified front glazing assembly is not part of the rear structure or rear-impact protective features governed by this regulation.
This regulation covers M2 and M3 vehicles, whereas the windscreen is intended for an M1 passenger car.
No windscreen-mounted AEBS camera, sensor or associated optical interface is specified, so an AEBS integration requirement cannot be inferred.
